newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: W.Australia says labour law effective 2-3 months.
newsitem.headline: W.Australia says labour law effective 2-3 months.

text.p: Controversial changes to Western Australian industrial relations laws will not take effect for another 2-3 months, a government spokesman said on Friday.
The changes were guillotined through State Parliament Thursday night despite threats of continued industrial protest action and international trade sanctions.
A sit-in in the Legislative Council also forced the final vote in that House to be held in a Select Committee Room.
On Friday the Government spokesman said it will take "2-3 months" to draft the necessary regulations to give effect to the new legislation.

A Fremantle Port Authority spokesperson said the port had been affected by a stevedores stoppage between 3.30 p.m. (0530 GMT) on Thursday and 7 a.m. (2300 GMT) Friday morning but was now functioning normally. The stevedores' stoppage had delayed cargo handling on two vessels, the spokesperson said.
